description:
src/backend.rs:101-112 — CalendarsBackend::create_object rustdoc is three lines:

    /// Create a new object of type `O`.
    ///
    /// Returns `(assigned_id, created_object)` on success. `create_id` is the
    /// client-side creation id used in the `/set` request.

The canonical mail-server's MailBackend::create_object at
crate-jmap-mail-server/src/backend.rs:59-104 documents two non-obvious
caller-side contracts:

    # Sentinel fields the backend MUST replace

    The method handlers in this crate pass partially-constructed objects
    with sentinel values that the backend MUST replace with real values
    before storing:

    - `id`: ... always set to `"placeholder"`. The backend MUST replace
      it with a real, unique, account-scoped ID ...

    - (mail-specific: blob_id, size)

    Failing to replace these sentinels will cause the client to receive
    invalid wire values.

    # Singleton types

    For types where only one instance may exist per account (e.g.,
    `VacationResponse`), `create_object` MUST be idempotent ... The
    `vacation.rs` handler relies on this guarantee to avoid a TOCTOU
    race ...

The calendars handler at src/event.rs in `handle_calendar_event_set`
passes the parsed CalendarEvent to create_object — does the handler set
`id` to "placeholder" before passing? (Per ic0j.10 in this epic, yes —
the placeholder hack exists.) The calendars trait doc doesn't say so.
A backend author reading the calendars trait doc has no way to know:

  - Whether the `id` field arrives populated with a sentinel or empty
  - Whether the backend MUST overwrite it or MUST preserve it
  - What happens if the backend keeps the placeholder string

What goes wrong for the caller: a calendars backend author looks at the
CalendarEvent passed in, sees `id: Id::from("placeholder")`, decides
"that looks deliberate, the client sent this, I'll preserve it". The
backend then stores an event with id = "placeholder". Subsequent
CalendarEvent/get fetches return the placeholder id verbatim to clients.
This is exactly the failure mode the mail-server doc warns about.

Fix: mirror the canonical doc structure. Document:

  - What sentinel values (if any) the handler passes in for `id`,
    `calendarIds`, or other fields.
  - That the backend MUST replace them and return the real id as
    the first tuple element.
  - Whether singleton or idempotency contracts apply (probably not
    for CalendarEvent, but worth saying so).

Note ic0j.10 in this epic already covers the placeholder-id mechanism
itself; this finding is about documenting it on the trait so backend
authors don't recreate the same footgun.

P3 — doc-as-contract gap; backend authors who only read create_object's
rustdoc may misimplement.
title: create_object rustdoc lacks 'sentinel fields the backend MUST replace' contract that canonical documents
